TEXT.English: Replaces the Warrior. Gains +50% forest defense.
TEXT.French: Remplace le guerrier. Gagne +50% de défense en forêt.
TEXT.Italian: Sostituisce il guerriero. Ottiene +50% difesa nelle foreste.
TEXT.Spanish: Sustituye al guerrero. Obtiene +50% de defensa en bosques.

TEXT.English: Lead the Adena communities of the Ohio Valley. Settle beside the rivers, cultivate native crops and build the earthworks that unite your people.
TEXT.French: Dirigez les communautés adena de la vallée de l'Ohio. Installez-vous près des rivières, cultivez les plantes locales et construisez les tertres qui unissent votre peuple.
TEXT.German: Führt die Adena-Gemeinschaften des Ohiotals. Siedelt an Flüssen, baut heimische Nutzpflanzen an und errichtet die Erdbauten, die euer Volk verbinden.
TEXT.Italian: Guidate le comunità adena della valle dell'Ohio. Insediatevi lungo i fiumi, coltivate piante locali e costruite i terrapieni che uniscono il vostro popolo.
TEXT.Spanish: Guía a las comunidades adena del valle del Ohio. Asiéntate junto a los ríos, cultiva plantas nativas y construye los terraplenes que unen a tu pueblo.

TEXT.English: Adena is an archaeological name for Early Woodland communities of the Ohio Valley and neighboring regions. These communities cultivated native plants, traded over long distances and built burial mounds. This civilization represents related communities rather than a single documented state. In the 800 BC scenario it shares the regional player slot used by the Mississippians in other scenarios, but remains Adena throughout the game and uses standard victories. Its river-farm production bonus represents community labor. The Wheel is included only as a game-tree prerequisite for Pottery.

TEXT.English: The Woodland Warrior represents local fighters familiar with the wooded valleys of eastern North America. It is a gameplay abstraction, not a documented Adena military order. It replaces the Warrior at the same cost and strength, with an additional 50% defense in forests.

TEXT.English: Adena communities constructed earthen burial mounds associated with mortuary ceremonies and community gathering. The Burial Mound replaces the Monument, retaining its culture and adding one happiness. It has the same cost, Mysticism requirement and Calendar obsolescence as the Monument.
